mainTopic: Finishing the definition of a שוטה, then the sources for who is exempt from ראייה: women, טומטום, אנדרוגינוס, minors, slaves, and the lame, blind, sick, and old.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב הונא's view that a שוטה must show all three crazy signs, like an ox that becomes מועד after goring three kinds of animals. רב פפא says a ברייתא giving one single sign would have changed רב הונא's mind. The גמרא asks whether that change covers only tearing clothes or all the signs, and the question ends in תיקו. Next, a ברייתא reads the פסוק about ראייה word by word. 'זכור' excludes women, 'זכורך' excludes a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס, and 'כל זכורך' includes minors. The גמרא explains why each lesson is needed, and finds that minors are included only מדרבנן, so 'כל זכורך' really teaches the view of אחרים about workers with smelly jobs. Then רב הונא learns that slaves are exempt from 'אל פני האדון', and רבינא shows that this פסוק is needed for a half-slave, half-free person. Finally a ברייתא learns from ״רגלים״ that the lame, blind, sick, and old are exempt, and רבא begins to explain what the extra phrase adds. His answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The goring ox comparison for a שוטה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's view ends with a comparison: a person who does three different crazy acts is like an ox that gored three different animals and became מועד for everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like an ox that gored an ox, a donkey, and a camel, and so became forewarned for every kind of animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רב הונא's explanation of why a שוטה needs all three signs. He compares it to the laws of a goring ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox that gores three different kinds of animals shows it is a goring animal in general, not just against one kind. In the same way, three different crazy acts show the person is truly unstable, not acting for some hidden reason.

keyTerms.meaning: gored
an ox known to be dangerous because it has gored repeatedly
for everything / for all kinds

phrases.english: like one that gored an ox, a donkey, and a camel,
phrases.notes: This finishes רב הונא's statement from the previous page, where he says a שוטה must do all three crazy acts together.

phrases.english: and became forewarned for all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends רב הונא's reasoning, which started on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three different crazy acts together set a person as a שוטה, just like three different gorings make an ox מועד for everything.

steps.title: רב פפא: a ברייתא would have changed רב הונא's mind
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that if רב הונא had known a ברייתא defining a שוטה as someone who destroys whatever he is given, he would have taken back his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If רב הונא had heard what the ברייתא teaches, that a שוטה is someone who destroys everything given to him, he would have changed his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on רב הונא by pointing to a ברייתא that gives one single sign of a שוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא needed three signs. The ברייתא shows that one behavior, destroying whatever you are given, is already enough. So רב הונא's requirement of all three signs looks too strict.

keyTerms.meaning: he heard / he knew of
that is taught in a ברייתא
a mentally unstable person, exempt from מצוות
he would have retracted

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
If Rav Huna had heard
that which is taught in a baraita:
Who is an imbecile?

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַמְאַבֵּד כׇּל מַה שֶּׁנּוֹתְנִים לוֹ,
phrases.english: This is one who destroys everything that is given to him,
he would have retracted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ לְרַב הוּנָא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's three-sign rule from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that all three signs are needed to be a שוטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא names a single behavior as enough to make someone a שוטה, so three signs are not always needed.

steps.title: How much would רב הונא have changed his mind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב הונא would only accept tearing clothes as a sign on its own, since it is like destroying things, or whether he would accept each of the signs on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: When רב הונא would change his mind, is it only about the one who tears his clothes, since that is like destroying what he is given? Or would he change his mind about all the signs?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how far רב פפא's point goes: does it change only one sign, or all of them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing clothes looks very much like 'destroying what is given to him,' so maybe only that sign now works alone. But maybe the ברייתא shows that any single crazy behavior is enough, which would cancel the three-sign rule for every sign.

keyTerms.meaning: it was asked of them (an open question)
one who tears his clothes
since it is similar to this
or perhaps

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
When he would have retracted,

phrases.aramaic: מִמְּקָרֵע כְּסוּתוֹ הוּא דַּהֲוָה הָדַר בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: is it from the one who tears his garment that he would have retracted,
since it is similar to this,
phrases.notes: "This" means the ברייתא's case of destroying whatever he is given.

phrases.english: or perhaps he would have retracted from all of them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: כִּי הֲוָה הָדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the reach of רב פפא's claim in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ברייתא make only tearing clothes enough on its own, or every one of the three signs?

steps.title: The question stays open
steps.stepSummary: The question is left unanswered: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds no answer and leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means we do not know which side is right. So it stays unclear whether one sign alone, other than tearing clothes, is enough to make someone a שוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand; the question stays unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא needs three signs for a שוטה. רב פפא says a ברייתא with one sign would have made him change his mind. Whether that change covers only tearing clothes or all the signs is left as תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 3 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Unresolved: we do not know if רב הונא would have dropped the three-sign rule for all the signs or only for tearing clothes.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: טומטום and אנדרוגינוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה: a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are exempt from ראייה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: And a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new part of the משנה. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed people exempt from going up to the בית המקדש on the רגלים. Now the גמרא will look for the source for exempting a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס.

keyTerms.meaning: a person whose gender is hidden and unknown
a person with both male and female features
etc.; the quote from the משנה continues

phrases.english: And a tumtum and a hermaphrodite, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שוטה topic and turns to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are exempt from ראייה.

steps.title: The ברייתא reads the words of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that "זכור" excludes women, "זכורך" excludes טומטום and אנדרוגינוס, and "כל זכורך" includes minors.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "Males" excludes women. "Your males" excludes a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס. "All your males" includes minors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the source for the משנה's exemptions, one word of the פסוק at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each extra word in the פסוק teaches something new. "זכור" leaves out women. The added "ך" (your) leaves out the טומטום and the אנדרוגינוס. The word "כל" adds young boys.

keyTerms.meaning: the רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
your males
to exclude
to include
minors

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Males" comes to exclude women.
"Your males" comes to exclude a tumtum and a hermaphrodite.
"All your males" comes to include the minors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source from the פסוק for the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women, טומטום and אנדרוגינוס are exempt from ראייה, and minors are included, based on the words זכור, זכורך, and כל זכורך.

steps.title: Why is a פסוק needed to exempt women?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the line "זכור excludes women" and asks why a פסוק is needed, since ראייה is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא and women are already exempt from those.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: "Males" excludes women. Why do I need a פסוק for this? It is a positive מצוה tied to a set time, and women are exempt from every positive מצוה tied to a set time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats one line of the ברייתא and challenges it: the פסוק seems to teach something we already know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראייה happens only on the רגלים, so it is tied to a set time. There is a general rule that women are exempt from such מצוות. So the word "זכור" seems unnecessary for exempting women.

keyTerms.meaning: the Master said (quoting a line from the ברייתא)
why do I need a פסוק?
after all / since
a positive מצוה tied to a set time
exempt (feminine plural)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא agrees that women are exempt. It is only asking why the פסוק is needed to teach that, since the general rule already does.

phrases.english: The Master said:
"Males" comes to exclude women.
Why do I need a verse for this?

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדִי מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא הוּא,
phrases.english: After all, it is a positive מצוה that is caused by time,
and from every positive מצוה caused by time
women are exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לְמָה לִי קְרָא? מִכְּדִי מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the first line of the ברייתא from step 6 in order to challenge it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of "זכור" to exempt women.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general rule exempting women from מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא already covers ראייה, so the פסוק seems unneeded.

steps.title: Why women need their own exclusion: we might have compared ראייה to הקהל
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is needed, because without it we might learn from the shared word 'ראייה' that, just like at הקהל, women are obligated in ראייה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. Otherwise you might think we should learn 'ראייה' from 'ראייה' at הקהל. Just as women are obligated in הקהל, they would be obligated here too. So the פסוק teaches us that they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 7: why do we need a פסוק to exempt women from ראייה? Without it, we might have obligated them by comparing ראייה to הקהל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule exempting women from a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא is not enough here. הקהל is also time-bound, yet women are obligated in it, and it shares the word 'ראייה' with our מצוה. So the פסוק 'זכור' blocks that comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed (the פסוק is not extra)
You might have thought (introduces the mistaken idea)
The gathering of all ישראל every seven years to hear the תורה read
So it teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying women are obligated in ראייה. It is saying the פסוק was needed to stop us from wrongly obligating them through a comparison to הקהל.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
since it could enter your mind to say:
let us learn 'appearance' from 'appearance' at the assembly (הקהל);
phrases.notes: הקהל also uses the word 'to appear' (דברים 31:11), so the shared word could link the two מצוות.

phrases.english: just as there women are obligated,
so too here women are obligated;
so the verse teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the פסוק is needed to block a possible גזירה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learn ראייה from הקהל through the shared word, so women would be obligated
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זכור' teaches that women are exempt from ראייה

steps.title: Why would a פסוק be needed to exclude a טומטום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the exclusion of an אנדרוגינוס is needed, but asks why a פסוק is needed to exclude a טומטום, whose status is only a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'זכורך' excludes a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס. The אנדרוגינוס makes sense: you might think that since he has a male side, he should be obligated. So the פסוק teaches that he is a separate kind of person. But a טומטום is only a doubt. Do we need a פסוק to exclude a doubt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא. It agrees the אנדרוגינוס needed a פסוק, but challenges why the טומטום did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אנדרוגינוס clearly has male features, so a פסוק is needed to show he is a category of his own. A טומטום is simply unknown: he might be male or female. We would not obligate someone who might not be male anyway, so the פסוק seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (quoting a line from the ברייתא)
Granted, this part makes sense (the first half of a challenge)
A male side or male aspect
A being of its own kind, neither male nor female
A doubt or uncertain case

phrases.english: The Master said: 'Your males'
comes to exclude a tumtum and a hermaphrodite.
Granted, for a hermaphrodite it was necessary,
since it could enter your mind to say:
since he has a male aspect,
he should be obligated;
so the verse teaches us
that he is a being unto himself.
But a tumtum is an uncertainty;
phrases.notes: A טומטום's body is covered, so we just don't know if he is male or female.

phrases.english: is a verse needed to exclude an uncertainty?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the ברייתא from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'זכורך' to exclude a טומטום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A doubtful case would not be obligated anyway, so a פסוק to exclude it seems pointless

steps.title: אביי: the טומטום here is one who is certainly male
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ברייתא means a טומטום whose testicles are visible. He is definitely male, so a פסוק is needed to exempt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it is talking about a case where his testicles are on the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by narrowing down which טומטום the ברייתא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the testicles are visible, he is surely male, so this is not a doubt. Even so, the פסוק teaches that he is exempt from ראייה, which we would not have known on our own.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers several questions here
His testicles are visible on the outside

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is when his testicles are on the outside.
phrases.notes: So he is surely male, and the פסוק still exempts him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A טומטום is only a doubt, so no פסוק is needed
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means a טומטום who is certainly male, and the פסוק exempts him

steps.title: 'כל זכורך' includes minors, but the משנה exempts a קטן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 'כל זכורך' includes minors, but our משנה lists a קטן among those exempt from ראייה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'כל זכורך' comes to include minors. But we learned in the משנה: everyone is obligated except a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last line of the ברייתא and points out that it seems to contradict our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא obligates minors from a פסוק, while the משנה clearly exempts a קטן. Both cannot be true as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: To include
But didn't we learn in a משנה? (introduces a contradiction)
A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor

phrases.english: The Master said: 'All your males'
comes to include the minors.
But didn't we learn in the משנה:
except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the last line of the ברייתא from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that 'כל זכורך' includes minors
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It contradicts the משנה, which exempts a קטן

steps.title: אביי: two different kinds of minors
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the ברייתא means a minor old enough for חינוך, and the משנה means a minor who is not yet old enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: this is not difficult. Here it means a minor who has reached the age of חינוך. There it means a minor who has not reached the age of חינוך.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי settles the contradiction by saying the two sources are talking about minors of different ages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child old enough to be trained in מצוות is included by the ברייתא. A child too young for training is the one the משנה exempts.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (the contradiction can be solved)
Here... there (each source is about a different case)
Training a child in מצוות

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult:
here, with a minor who has reached the age of training;
there, with a minor who has not reached the age of training.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and the משנה talk about the same minors and contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means a minor at the age of חינוך, and the משנה means one below it

steps.title: But חינוך is only a rabbinic obligation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: the obligation of a minor at the age of חינוך is only דרבנן, so how can a פסוק teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But a minor who has reached the age of חינוך is only obligated by rabbinic law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's answer. If חינוך is a rabbinic rule, a פסוק in the תורה should not be the source for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns the rule about minors from 'כל זכורך', which sounds like a תורה law. But training children is a rule of the חכמים, so the source and the rule do not match.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule from the חכמים, not from the תורה itself

phrases.english: A minor who has reached the age of training,
his obligation is only by rabbinic law!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading that the ברייתא's 'כל זכורך' refers to a minor at the age of חינוך
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic obligation cannot truly come from a פסוק

steps.title: Yes, and the פסוק is only an אסמכתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the obligation is rabbinic and says the פסוק is just a support for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. The פסוק is just a support for the rabbinic rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and explains that the ברייתא's use of the פסוק is only an אסמכתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The minor's obligation really comes from the חכמים. The ברייתא hangs it on 'כל זכורך' only as a hint or support, not as a true תורה source, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so
Just a support: a rabbinic rule hinted at in a פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: From the ברייתא on 'זכור / זכורך / כל זכורך': women need a פסוק so we don't learn from הקהל. The טומטום who is excluded is one who is certainly male. Minors at the age of חינוך are included only מדרבנן, and the פסוק is an אסמכתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in ש״ס: a ברייתא may cite a פסוק for something that is really a rabbinic rule, using the פסוק only as an אסמכתא.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so,
and the verse is a mere support.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, וּקְרָא אַסְמַכְתָּא בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by accepting it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the premise and reframes the פסוק as an אסמכתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's פסוק seemed to be a real תורה source for obligating minors
steps.terutzMaskana: The obligation is rabbinic, and the פסוק is only a support
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A minor at the age of חינוך is obligated in ראייה מדרבנן, and 'כל זכורך' is an אסמכתא.

steps.title: So what does the verse come to teach?
steps.stepSummary: If 'כל זכורך' is only a support for a rabbinic rule about minors, what does the פסוק itself actually teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what does the verse come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the words 'כל זכורך' really teach, now that the minor rule turned out to be only rabbinic. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 the גמרא said the פסוק is only a support for the rabbinic rule about a minor at the age of חינוך. The תורה does not waste words, so the word 'כל' must still teach some real law מדאורייתא. The גמרא now looks for it.

keyTerms.meaning: A verse (a פסוק)
What does it come to teach?

phrases.english: But then, what does the verse come for?
phrases.notes: The verse is 'כל זכורך', which the ברייתא in step 6 used to include minors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 14: if the פסוק is only a support, its real lesson from the תורה is still missing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The real lesson מדאורייתא of the words 'כל זכורך'.

steps.title: The verse teaches the view of אחרים about people with smelly jobs
steps.stepSummary: 'כל זכורך' teaches that only someone who can travel up together with all the other men is obligated. People with very smelly jobs are excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes for the view of אחרים. As we learned: אחרים say that a dung collector, a copper refiner, and a tanner are exempt from ראייה, because it says 'all your males.' That means someone who can go up together with all your males. These people are excluded, because they are not fit to go up with all your males.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'כל זכורך' teaches the opinion of אחרים: workers whose jobs leave a bad smell are exempt from ראייה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כל' (all) is read as 'together with everyone.' A person who cannot comfortably join the whole group is left out. These workers smell so bad that others avoid them, so the תורה does not obligate them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others': the name used for a תנא whose name is not given
One who collects dog dung for tanning hides
One who refines copper
A tanner of hides
The מצוה of appearing in the בית המקדש on the רגלים

phrases.english: For the view of אחרים. As we learned: אחרים say:
A dung collector,
phrases.notes: Someone who gathers dog dung and sells it to tanners, a very smelly job.

phrases.english: and a copper refiner, and a tanner —
are exempt from the appearance-מצוה,
because it says: 'All your males,'

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיָּכוֹל לַעֲלוֹת עִם כׇּל זְכוּרְךָ.
phrases.english: meaning one who is able to go up with all your males.
These are excluded, since they are not fit
to go up with all your males.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 by giving the פסוק a new lesson מדאורייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כל זכורך' teaches that only someone who can join the whole group must go up, which exempts workers with very smelly jobs.
steps.whatToRemember: 'כל זכורך' is a support for the rabbinic rule about a minor at the age of חינוך. Its real lesson from the תורה is the view of אחרים: people others cannot travel with, like tanners, are exempt from ראייה.

steps.title: Women are exempt, but where do we learn that slaves are exempt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's exemption of women and unfreed slaves and asks for the source for slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Women and slaves who are not freed, etc.' Women are fine, as we said earlier. But slaves, where do we learn that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next case in the משנה, women and unfreed slaves. It asks for a source for exempting slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption of women already has a source: the ברייתא's word 'זכור' (males) leaves out women. Slaves are men, though, so that word does not exclude them. The גמרא needs a separate source for them.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaves who are not freed
It is fine / understandable (about one case)
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: Women and slaves who are not freed, etc.
Women are fine, as we said,
but slaves, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא נָשִׁים כְּדַאֲמַרַן, אֶלָּא עֲבָדִים מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that exempts slaves from ראייה.

steps.title: רב הונא: a slave has another master
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא learns from 'before the Master, ה׳' that only someone with one Master is obligated. A slave has a human master too, so he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: the verse says 'before the Master, ה׳.' That means someone who has only one Master. This excludes a slave, who has another master.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a פסוק as the source that slaves are exempt from ראייה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls ה׳ 'the Master.' רב הונא reads this as speaking to people whose only master is ה׳. A slave also belongs to a human master, so he is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Master
This one is excluded

phrases.english: רב הונא said: the verse says:
'Before the Master, ה׳' —

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא אָדוֹן אֶחָד,
phrases.english: meaning one who has only one Master,

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא זֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אָדוֹן אַחֵר.
phrases.english: which excludes this one, who has another master.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17's question with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אל פני האדון ה׳' exempts anyone who has another master besides ה׳, meaning a slave.

steps.title: Why is a verse needed? A slave already follows a woman's rules
steps.stepSummary: A slave is obligated only in the מצוות a woman is obligated in, learned from the matching words 'לה לה'. Women are exempt from ראייה, so slaves should be exempt without a new פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a verse for this? After all, any מצוה a woman is obligated in, a slave is obligated in. Any מצוה a woman is not obligated in, a slave is not obligated in. We learn this from 'לה' and 'לה' about a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא: his פסוק seems unnecessary, because a known rule already exempts slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that a slave's מצוה obligations match a woman's. It is learned from a גזירה שוה on the word 'לה'. Women are exempt from ראייה, so slaves should be exempt automatically, and רב הונא's פסוק adds nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need a verse for this?
After all / since
He learns it from the word 'לה' appearing in both places (a גזירה שוה)

phrases.english: Why do I need a verse for this?

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי כׇּל מִצְוָה שֶׁהָאִשָּׁה חַיֶּיבֶת בָּהּ —
phrases.english: After all, any מצוה that a woman is obligated in —
a slave is obligated in it,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִצְוָה שֶׁאֵין הָאִשָּׁה חַיֶּיבֶת בָּהּ —
phrases.english: any מצוה that a woman is not obligated in —
a slave is not obligated in it,
since he learns 'to her,' 'to her,' from a woman!
phrases.notes: 'לה' is said about a slave woman (ויקרא 19:20) and about a divorced wife (דברים 24:3), which links their rules.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's source as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's use of 'אל פני האדון ה׳' to exempt slaves.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'לה לה' rule already gives slaves the same exemptions as women, and women are exempt from ראייה, so a new פסוק is not needed.

steps.title: רבינא: the verse is for someone half-slave, half-free
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the פסוק is needed only for a person who is half-slave and half-free.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: the verse is needed only for someone who is half slave and half free.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends רב הונא by saying his פסוק covers a case the 'לה לה' rule does not cover: a half-slave, half-free person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'לה לה' rule covers a regular slave. A person who is half free is a different case, and that rule alone would not settle it. The פסוק 'one Master' teaches that he is exempt too, because he still partly has a human master.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for…
Half slave and half free person

phrases.english: רבינא said: it is needed only

phrases.aramaic: לְמִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין.
phrases.english: for one who is half slave and half free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 by narrowing the פסוק to a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the פסוק to a case the general rule does not cover
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to repeat what the 'לה לה' rule already teaches about slaves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is needed for a half-slave, half-free person, who is also exempt from ראייה.

steps.title: The משנה's wording supports רבינא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says 'slaves who are not freed.' Since plain 'slaves' would have been enough, the extra words must mean slaves who are not fully freed, which is the half-slave case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is exact too, because it teaches: 'Women and slaves who are not freed.' What does 'who are not freed' mean? If you say it means not freed at all, it should just say 'slaves.' So doesn't it mean not freed completely? And who is that? Someone who is half slave and half free. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the extra words in the משנה, 'who are not freed,' support רבינא's half-slave case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave who is not freed at all is simply called a 'slave,' so the extra words must be there for a reason. They point to someone who is not fully freed, meaning a half-slave, half-free person. This proves the משנה also exempts him, just as רבינא said.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact (and supports this)
If you say
Plainly, with no added description
Completely
Learn from this (the point is proven)

phrases.english: The wording is exact too, because it teaches:
'Women and slaves who are not freed.'
What does 'who are not freed' mean?
If you say: not freed at all —
then let it just teach 'slaves' plainly!
Rather, doesn't it mean not freed completely?
And who are they?

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין.
phrases.english: One who is half slave and half free.
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבינא's answer from the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's claim that a half-slave, half-free person is exempt from ראייה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra words 'שאינן משוחררין' in our משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: Women are exempt from ראייה because of 'זכור'. A full slave is exempt because a slave follows a woman's rules ('לה לה'). רב הונא's פסוק 'אל פני האדון' is needed for a half-slave, half-free person, and the משנה's words 'שאינן משוחררין' point to him.

steps.title: The lame, blind, sick and old are exempt: the source from ״רגלים״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list of the lame, blind, sick, and old. It brings a ברייתא that learns from ״רגלים״ to exclude people with artificial legs. A second reading of the same word excludes the lame, sick, blind, old, and anyone who cannot go up on his own feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the lame, the blind, the sick, and the old are exempt. The רבנן taught: the פסוק says ״רגלים״, which hints at feet. This excludes people with artificial legs. Another explanation: ״רגלים״ excludes the lame, the sick, the blind, the old, and one who cannot go up on his own feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that gives their source in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״רגלים״ in the פסוק means 'times' (festival times), but it sounds like רגליים, feet. So the ברייתא reads it as 'a מצוה for those who go up on their feet.' The first reading uses this to exclude someone with artificial legs, even though he can walk. The second reading uses it to exclude the whole list from the משנה, plus one more category.

keyTerms.meaning: A lame person
A blind person
'Times' (festivals). The ברייתא reads it as hinting at רַגְלַיִם, feet
People with artificial or wooden legs
Another explanation: a second way to read the same words

steps.confusionAlert: Both readings use the same word ״רגלים״. The ברייתא is not quoting two different פסוקים. It is offering two different ways to learn from one word.

phrases.english: And the lame, and the blind, and the sick, and the old.
The Rabbis taught: "Times (regalim)"
phrases.notes: שמות 23:14. The word sounds like 'feet' (רגליים), and that's the hint being used.

phrases.english: excludes people with artificial legs!
Another explanation: "regalim"
excludes the lame and the sick
and the blind and the old
and one who is unable to go up on his feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the slave discussion behind and opens the next items in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From ״רגלים״ (feet): only those who can go up on their own healthy feet are obligated in ראייה. People with artificial legs are excluded, and so are the lame, sick, blind, old, and anyone unable to go up on his feet.

steps.title: What does 'one who cannot go up on his feet' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra case the ברייתא's last category includes. The lame and the sick were already listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said 'one who cannot go up on his feet.' What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא added a final, general category after already listing specific cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone lame or sick obviously cannot go up on his feet, and those cases were already named. So the general phrase seems extra. The גמרא assumes it must include some new person not already covered.

keyTerms.meaning: To include, to bring in an extra case
What?

phrases.english: "And one who is unable to go up on his feet"
comes to include what?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לַעֲלוֹת בְּרַגְלָיו לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the last phrase of the ברייתא quoted in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new case is added by 'one who cannot go up on his feet' that the lame and sick do not already cover?

steps.title: רבא begins to explain what the extra phrase includes
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts to answer that the phrase comes to include an extra case. His full answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it comes to include...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins his answer to the question of what the extra category adds. The rest of his words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא accepts the question's starting point: the phrase is not extra wording but adds a real new case. Which case that is will be stated in the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question here

phrases.english: Rava said: to include...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא says the phrase includes an additional case. The specific case appears in the continuation of the text.
